lessons: Checks were green and the fence held. Review snagged on one assertion only: tests/test_seeded_phase4_05.py:108 asserts `not (REPO / path).exists()` for phase4-exit's new paths. Keep the rest of the diff and the authored phase4-exit ticket.

Delete the live-repo exists() check. phase4-exit creates tests/test_phase4_exit.py and tests/test_seeded_phase5_core.py, and its fence cannot edit this file, so the check turns the full suite red for the successor.

Prove new-path ownership through fences and Context alone: the path is in the owner's scope_fence, absent from the other stem's fence, and absent from every Context. If you want a non-existence proof, use tmp_path built from EXISTING_AT_AUTHORING, as in test_seeded_phase4_01.py:177.

Before submitting, look for any other assertion that must stay true after phase4-exit merges its outputs. Checks against live REPO state that phase4-exit will change (new files, a new ticket dir) must be pinned to authoring-time fixtures instead.
This supersedes the earlier lesson 'The exit-owned paths must not exist on disk yet.' Prove that invariant only through a fixture, never through the live repo.
reason: One fixable oversight: a live-repo non-existence assertion that the successor would break. The reviewer gave a concrete paved road, so retry at the same capability.
